# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1012

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃1012화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|쉼 없이 내달리는 말발굽을 따라, 시간은 바람처럼 스쳐 지나갔다.
  6|
  7|석양이 광야를 집어삼키고, 이내 찾아온 어둠이 세상을 짓누를 때까지. 뒤이어 어스름한 여명이 그 사이를 비집고 번져올 때까지.
  8|
  9|그리고 두 번째로 찾아온 어둠이 깊어졌을 때, 쉴 틈 없이 달싹이던 마중걸의 입술도 마침내 휴식을 취할 수 있었다.
 10|
 11|“……그렇게 된 겁니다.”
 12|
 13|긴 이야기를 끝마친 마중걸은 하룻밤 사이에 폭삭 늙어 있었다.
 14|
 15|지난 십여 년간 있었던 일들을 꼬박 하루가 넘게 줄줄 읊어서이기도 했지만, 그보다는 나를 시작으로 하나씩 늘어난 청중(聽衆)들로 인한 부담감이 더욱 컸을 것이다.
 16|
 17|물론 그중에서도 특히, 화왕(火王)이라는 거인에게서 뿜어져 나오는 압박감은 말할 것도 없었다.
 18|
 19|“그렇게 되긴 뭐가 돼. 더 지껄여 보거라.”
 20|
 21|나지막한 적천강의 윽박지름에, 가뜩이나 녹초가 되어 있던 마중걸이 울상을 지어 보였다.
 22|
 23|“진짜 끝입니다. 이제 더는 말할 것도 없다니까요.”
 24|
 25|“지금부터 뒤져서 나오면 한 음절에 열 대다. 이래도 없느냐?”
 26|
 27|“예?”
 28|
 29|아니, 무슨 썰 보따리가 있는 것도 아닌데 뒤지긴 뭘 뒤져.
 30|
 31|마중걸의 애처로운 눈빛을 받은 나는 고개를 절레절레 내저으며 입을 열었다.
 32|
 33|“그만하시죠. 그리고 한 음절에 백 대면 미쳤다고 말합니까? 설령 남은 이야기가 있더라도 죽을 각오로 버티지.”
 34|
 35|“그래? 그럼 열 대로 낮춰 줄 테니 싹 다 털어놔라.”
 36|
 37|“그 정도만 해도 충분히 죽어요.”
 38|
 39|“좋다. 한 대. 노부의 마지막 제안이다.”
 40|
 41|“……차라리 마지막 유언을 하라고 하십쇼. 이쯤 되면 그냥 죽이고 싶어 하시는 것 같은데.”
 42|
 43|내 조곤조곤한 반박에 적천강이 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
 44|
 45|“네 녀석은 너무 물러터졌다. 이렇게라도 해야 뭐든 한 마디라도 더 쥐어 짜내지.”
 46|
 47|“저 양반 꼴을 좀 보세요. 이제는 쥐어 짜내도 육수 한 방울 안 나옵니다.”
 48|
 49|그냥 하는 말이 아니라, 지금의 마중걸은 반쯤 영혼이 빠져나가 있는 상태나 다름없었다.
 50|
 51|생각해 보라.
 52|
 53|말이 쉬워서 십 년이지, 강산도 변하는 그 긴 세월 동안 있었던 모든 일을 잠 한숨 못 자고 세세하게 떠올려야 했으니 하루 조금 넘는 시간 만에 반건조 오징어가 될 수밖에 없었다.
 54|
 55|“미, 믿어 주십시오. 저는 진짜 하나도 안 빼놓고 전부 말씀드렸습니다.”
 56|
 57|마중걸이 그렁그렁해진 눈으로 애원하듯 말하자, 그의 여섯 의형제도 덩달아 입을 열었다.
 58|
 59|아니, 정확히는 열다가 말았다.
 60|
 61|“대형께서 하신 말씀이 맞…….”
 62|
 63|“처맞기 전에 전부 주둥이 닥쳐라. 특히 네놈.”
 64|
 65|적천강에 의해 지목된 난쟁이가 바짝 얼어붙었다.
 66|
 67|“저, 저 말입니까?”
 68|
 69|“그래. 앞으로 한 번만 더 갈갈거리면 뒈질 줄 알아라. 말 한마디 끝날 때마다 뭔 추임새 넣는 것도 아니고, 어린 놈의 새끼가.”
 70|
 71|적천강의 일갈에 난쟁이가 입을 꾹 다물자, 그 광경을 옆에서 지켜보던 주먹코가 희열에 찬 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
 72|
 73|“드디어…….”
 74|
 75|드디어는 뭐가 드디어야.
 76|
 77|이놈이나 저놈이나 제정신이 아닌 것 같지만, 여하튼 하나는 확실해졌다.
 78|
 79|“무진아.”
 80|
 81|내 부름에 담긴 의미를 알아차린 혁무진이 입맛을 다셨다.
 82|
 83|전날부터 흑룡마문과 함께하게 된 사마표, 태산을 제외한 다른 대원들 역시 반응은 엇비슷했다.
 84|
 85|“씁. 괜찮을까요? 영 찝찝한데.”
 86|
 87|“은인, 아니 진 공자, 아니 각주님.”
 88|
 89|“포박이라도 하는 게 좋을 듯싶은데.”
 90|
 91|“내 생각은 좀 다르…… 제기랄. 이 빌어먹을 말안장!”
 92|
 93|안락하기 그지없던 태산의 어깨와는 달리, 거칠게 들썩이는 말안장 위에서 엉덩이 통증을 호소하던 남호가 찡그린 얼굴로 말을 이었다.
 94|
 95|“각주 지시를 따라야지. 그게 맞아. 그리고 뭐 굳이 포박하거나 하지 않아도 저놈들이 언감생심 딴 마음을 품을 수나 있겠나?”
 96|
 97|“그것도 그러네요.”
 98|
 99|고개를 끄덕여 수긍한 혁무진을 시작으로, 주화란과 송일섬도 각자 쥐고 있던 말고삐를 놓았다.
100|
101|물론 그 말고삐는 그들 자신의 것이 아닌, 포위하듯 바짝 옆에 붙어 달리던 백마칠종(白馬七宗)의 것이었다.
102|
103|“믿어 줘서 고맙소.”
104|
105|“아직 완전히 믿는 건 아니니까 고마워하실 필요는 없고.”
106|
107|눈물까지 글썽이는 마중걸에게는 그렇게 대꾸했지만, 내 속마음은 달랐다.
108|
109|‘아무리 생각해 봐도 암천이 보낸 간자(間者)들은 아니야.’
110|
111|물론 처음 전음을 엿들었을 때만 해도 잠시 묻어 두었던 의심이 무럭무럭 솟아났었다.
112|
113|그러니까, 처음에는.
114|
115|하지만 마중걸의 이야기를 모두 들은 지금, 마음속 의심은 어느새 누군가를 향한 호기심으로 변해 있었다.
116|
117|마중걸과 그의 의형제들이 대인(大人)이라 부르며 떠받드는, 정체불명의 고수에 대한 호기심.
118|
119|- 어찌 생각하느냐.
120|
121|귓가를 파고드는 나지막한 전음.
122|
123|적천강의 물음에 담긴 의미를 이미 알고 있는 나는, 자연스럽게 고개를 돌려 전방을 주시하며 대답했다.
124|
125|- 글쎄요.
126|
127|- 말을 아끼는 것이냐. 아니면…….
128|
129|- 정말 잘 모르겠어서 드리는 말씀입니다. 대인이라는 그자, 수상하다기보다는 묘해요. 정말 희한할 정도로.
130|
131|과장이 아니라, 사실이 그랬다.
132|
133|어느 날 홀연히 나타나 관부의 통제마저 벗어난 마적단을 단숨에 일망타진한 의문의 초절정 고수, 이른바 대인은 그만큼 베일에 싸인 존재였으니까.
134|
135|‘이름도, 출신 내력도, 그 무엇하나 제대로 아는 게 없다고 했지.’
136|
137|백마칠종이 그를 모시기 시작한 지 무려 십여 년이다.
138|
139|그런데 마중걸은 물론 백마칠종 중 그 누구도 대인의 정체를 몰랐고, 그런 그들에게 추궁을 가할 때마다 이구동성으로 토해 낸 대답은 대부분 엇비슷했다.
140|
141|
142|
143|‘아니, 전부 사실입니다. 원래 그런 분이라니까요?’
144|
145|‘저희가 어느 안전이라고 감히 거짓을 아뢰겠습니까. 제발 좀 믿어 주십쇼.’
146|
147|‘저희가 나눈 대화를 들으셨다니 이미 아시겠지만 그분이 원래 좀, 아니 상당히 오락가락합니다. 예? 이름이랑 나이요? 말도 마십시오. 물어볼 때마다 달라집니다. 막내야, 안 그러냐?’
148|
149|‘형님들 말씀이 맞습니다. 칠복이, 개똥이…… 삼 년 전인가? 스스로를 열일곱 살 된 소향이로 알고 있더라고요. 그때부터 저희도 두 손 두 발 다 들었습니다.’
150|
151|‘녕하성에 언제부터 머물렀는지도 모르겠습니다. 그냥 갑자기 나타나서 말도 안 되는 신위(神威)로 인근을 평정하더니, 그 후로는 거처에 처박혀서 꿈쩍도 안 하지 뭡니까. 근 십 년을 그랬어요. 믿기지 않으시겠지만 사실입니다.’
152|
153|
154|
155|뽑아도 뽑아도 줄줄이 끌려 나오는 고구마 줄기처럼, 들을수록 황당한 이야기들이 우후죽순으로 쏟아졌다.
156|
157|듣던 와중에 문득 이런 생각이 들 수밖에 없을 만큼.
158|
159|‘그 인간, 도대체 뭐지?’
160|
161|누구에게나 탐욕은 있다.
162|
163|옳고 그른 방향인지를 떠나, 사람이라면 한 번쯤 마음속에 품은 목표가 존재하기 마련이니까.
164|
165|하지만 이야기 속의 대인은 어디에도 해당하지 않았다.
166|
167|녕하 일대를 손에 넣고 위풍당당한 패자(霸者)로 군림한 것도 아니요. 그렇다고 신분을 감추기 위해 변방으로 스며든 악명 높은 마두(魔頭)나 인생을 마무리하기 위해 아무도 찾지 않는 곳을 떠도는 은거기인(隱居伎人)도 아니었다.
168|
169|‘패자로 군림할 속셈이라면 곧장 동굴에 처박힐 이유가 없고, 마두였다면 정체가 발각될 테니 기를 쓰고 숨겼겠지. 아니면 처음부터 마적단들을 수하로 부리거나.’
170|
171|은거기인일 경우는 깊게 생각할 필요조차 없다.
172|
173|솔직히 어느 정신 나간 은거기인이 풍경 좋고 물 맑은 심산유곡(深山幽谷)을 놔두고 사시사철 미세먼지 농도 짙음에 황사가 불어오는 변방으로 향하겠나.
174|
175|무식한 나도 알 정도로 유명한 시인인 폴 발레리가 프랑스가 아닌 녕하성에 살았다면, ‘황사가 분다. 시발 죽고 싶다.’라고 했을 거다.
176|
177|‘심지어 늙어서 노망이 들었거나 심산유곡을 찾을 필요도 없이 죽을 날을 받아 둔 노인네냐, 하면 그것도 아니고.’
178|
179|백마칠종의 증언에 의하면, 대인은 워낙 씻지 않아 땟국물이 줄줄 흘렀음에도 대충 그 용모와 음성은 중년 어림.
180|
181|게다가 마중걸과 그 의형제들이 찾아와 술과 음식을 바치면 그 대가로 약간의 가르침을 베풀기도 하고, 거처에 머무르다가 가끔 한 번씩 마실까지 나간다고 했다.
182|
183|계속 안에만 있으면 답답하다고. 사람 냄새 좀 맡고 싶다고.
184|
185|얼마나 자주 싸돌아다녔으면, 백마칠종이 굳이 나서서 대인의 정체를 숨기지 않아도 자연스럽게 녕하성에 녹아들 정도라고 했다.
186|
187|거지1 정도의 느낌으로.
188|
189|‘이딴 게…… 은거기인?’
190|
191|깊은 수렁에 빠진다면 마치 이런 기분일까.
192|
193|생각할수록 어이없음과 호기심만 부풀어 가던 그때, 아마도 나와 같은 상념을 떠올린 것이 분명한 적천강이 입술을 달싹였다.
194|
195|- 노부가 이만하면 살기도 오래 살고, 미친놈들도 수백 수레쯤은 봤다고 생각했는데…… 이런 인간 군상은 머리털 나고 처음 본다.
196|
197|- 새로 나기 시작한 지 얼마 안 되셨잖아요.
198|
199|- ……뒈지고 싶으냐?
200|
201|- 아뇨. 그보다 노야께서 하신 말씀에는 저도 공감합니다. 도무지 종잡을 수가 없어요.
202|
203|- 천주, 그놈이 부리는 수족 중 하나일까?
204|
205|- 남아 있는 손발이야 당연히 있겠죠. 하지만 만약 노야께서 천주라면, 저런 인간을 수족으로 부리시겠습니까?
206|
207|적천강이 망설임 없이 대답했다.
208|
209|- 미쳤느냐?
210|
211|- 그렇죠?
212|
213|- 대가리에 멸염신권을 맞아도 그런 놈은 수하로 안 부린다. 물론, 저 흉악하게 생겨 먹은 놈들이 털어놓은 이야기가 모두 진실이라는 가정하에.
214|
215|- 그런데 이미 믿고 계시잖아요.
216|
217|- 그건…….
218|
219|흐려지는 전음과 함께 반사적으로 돌아가는 고개.
220|
221|시선을 마주치기가 무섭게 석상처럼 굳어 버리는 백마칠종의 모습에, 적천강이 고개를 절레절레 저었다.
222|
223|- 그래, 네 녀석의 생각이 맞느니라. 노부가 느끼기에도 저놈들은 거짓말을 하고 있지 않다. 아니, 그럴 깜냥조차 없어.
224|
225|이것 하나만큼은 내가 보기에도, 그리고 다른 모두가 보더라도 마찬가지일 것이다.
226|
227|하지만 저들과 대인의 존재가 아군에게 무해(無害)하다는 결론을 도출했다 한들, 우리 두 사람만의 직감으로 모든 것을 결정지을 수는 없는 법.
228|
229|- 어찌하겠느냐?
230|
231|적천강의 전음이 재차 귓가를 파고든 순간, 짧은 고민 끝에 판단을 내린 나는 말고삐를 서서히 늦추며 백마칠종과 말머리를 나란히 했다.
232|
233|“이, 이번에는 도대체 왜…….”
234|

- Do not censor or soften content.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

[P12]
“If I dig around and something else comes out, it’s ten hits per syllable. Still nothing?”

[P13]
“What?”

[P14]

[P15]

[P16]
“Give it a rest. And why would he say anything if it’s a hundred hits per syllable? Even if he had more to tell, he’d hold out to the death.”

[P17]
“Is that so? Then I’ll lower it to ten. Spill everything.”

[P18]
“Ten would still kill him.”

[P19]
“Fine. One hit. That’s this old man’s final offer.”

[P20]
“…You might as well ask for his last words. At this point, it sounds like you just want him dead.”

[P21]
Jeok Cheongang frowned at my quiet objection.

[P22]
“You’re too soft. Sometimes you have to squeeze a man to get even one more word out of him.”

[P23]
“Look at him. You couldn’t squeeze a drop of broth out of him now.”

[P24]
I wasn’t exaggerating. Ma Junggeol looked as if half his soul had left his body.

[P25]
Think about it.

[P26]
Ten years was easy to say. But he’d had to recall, in detail and without a wink of sleep, everything that had happened over a span long enough for mountains and rivers to change. No wonder he’d turned into a half-dried squid in just over a day.

[P27]
“P-please believe me. I really told you everything. I didn’t leave a thing out.”

[P28]
Ma Junggeol pleaded with tears in his eyes, and his six sworn brothers opened their mouths to back him up.

[P29]
Or rather, they started to.

[P30]
“What Eldest Brother said is righ—”

[P31]
“Shut your mouths before I beat you. Especially you.”

[P32]
The short one Jeok Cheongang had singled out froze.

[P33]
“M-me?”

[P34]
“Yes, you. Chatter like that one more time and you’re dead. Do you have to chime in after every sentence, you little brat?”

[P35]
The short one clamped his mouth shut. Watching from beside him, the bulbous-nosed one murmured with delight.

[P36]
“Finally…”

[P37]
Finally what?

[P38]
None of these men seemed quite right in the head, but one thing was clear.

[P39]
“Mujin.”

[P40]
Hyuk Mujin understood what I meant and clicked his tongue. The other members reacted much the same way, apart from Sama Pyo and Taishan, who’d joined us the day before along with the Black Dragon Demon Gate.

[P41]
“Tsk. Is this really okay? It doesn’t sit right with me.”

[P42]
“Benefactor—no, Young Master Jin—no, Pavilion Master.”

[P43]
“I think we should at least tie them up.”

[P44]
“I see it differently—damn it, this miserable saddle!”

[P45]
Namho had been comfortably riding on Taishan’s shoulders before. Now he was on a saddle that bounced beneath him, and his backside was paying for it. He grimaced and went on.

[P46]
“We should follow the Pavilion Master’s orders. That’s the right call. Besides, do you think those men would dare try anything, tied up or not?”

[P47]
“I suppose not.”

[P48]
Hyuk Mujin nodded. He, Ju Hwaran, and Song Ilseom let go of the reins they’d each been holding.

[P49]
Not their own reins, of course. They belonged to the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang, who had been riding close beside them, hemmed in on all sides.

[P50]
“Thank you for trusting us.”

[P51]
“I don’t trust you completely, so you don’t need to thank me.”

[P52]
That was what I told Ma Junggeol, whose eyes had filled with tears again. Privately, though, I thought otherwise.

[P53]
*No matter how I look at it, they’re not spies sent by Dark Heaven.*

[P54]
When I first overheard their Sound Transmission, the suspicions I’d set aside had come rushing back.

[P55]
At first, anyway.

[P56]
Now that I’d heard Ma Junggeol’s whole story, those suspicions had given way to curiosity about someone else.

[P57]
The mysterious master Ma Junggeol and his sworn brothers revered as Great Sir.

[P58]
—What do you think?

[P59]
Jeok Cheongang’s low Sound Transmission reached my ear. I knew what he was asking, so I turned my gaze toward the road ahead and answered.

[P60]
—I’m not sure.

[P61]
—Are you holding back? Or…

[P62]
—I really don’t know. The man they call Great Sir seems less suspicious than… strange. Unbelievably strange.

[P63]
That was no exaggeration.

[P64]
This mysterious Supreme Peak master had appeared out of nowhere one day and wiped out a band of mounted bandits beyond even the authorities’ control. Yet Great Sir himself remained shrouded in mystery.

[P65]
*They said they didn’t know his name, where he came from, or anything else about him.*

[P66]
The Seven Masters of Baekma Bang had served him for more than ten years. Yet none of them, Ma Junggeol included, knew who he was. Whenever we pressed them, their answers were much the same.

[P67]
*“No, it’s all true. That’s just what he’s like!”*

[P68]
*“We wouldn’t dare lie to you. Please believe us.”*

[P69]
*“You heard us talking, so you already know he’s a bit—no, more than a bit—all over the place. His name and age? Don’t even ask. They change every time. Isn’t that right, Youngest?”*

[P70]
*“My brothers are right. Chilbok, Gaettong… Was it three years ago? He thought he was a seventeen-year-old girl named Sohyang. That’s when we gave up trying to make sense of it.”*

[P71]
*“We don’t know when he came to Ningxia Province, either. He just appeared, subdued the whole area with power you’d have to see to believe, then shut himself away and barely moved for nearly ten years. I know it’s hard to believe, but it’s true.”*

[P72]
The absurd stories kept coming, like sweet potato vines that refused to end no matter how many you pulled up. Listening to them, I couldn’t help wondering:

[P73]
*What the hell is that guy?*

[P74]
Everyone wanted something.

[P75]
Right or wrong, everyone had some goal they’d held in their heart at least once.

[P76]
But Great Sir, as they described him, fit none of the possibilities.

[P77]
He hadn’t taken over Ningxia and ruled it as a mighty conqueror. Nor did he sound like a notorious fiend hiding his identity on the frontier, or a hermit master wandering where no one would find him as his life drew to a close.

[P78]
*If he wanted to rule, why hole up in a cave? If he were a fiend, he’d be desperate to keep his identity hidden before anyone recognized him. Or he’d have taken the mounted bandits as his followers from the start.*

[P79]
As for a hermit master, I hardly needed to think about it.

[P80]
What kind of deranged hermit would pass up a remote mountain valley with beautiful scenery and clear water to settle on a frontier where fine dust hung in the air and yellow sand blew through all year?

[P81]
Even an ignoramus like me knew the famous poet Paul Valéry. If he’d lived in Ningxia Province instead of France, he would’ve written, *The yellow dust is blowing. Fuck, I want to die.*

[P82]
*And it wasn’t as if he were some senile old man, or someone so close to death that finding a mountain valley wasn’t worth the trouble.*

[P83]
According to the Seven Masters, Great Sir washed so rarely that grime practically ran off him. Even so, what they could make out of his face and hear in his voice suggested a man around middle age.

[P84]
When Ma Junggeol and his sworn brothers brought him liquor and food, he sometimes gave them a little instruction in return. And though he mostly stayed at his residence, he went out for the occasional stroll.

[P85]
He said being inside all the time felt stifling. He wanted to smell other people for a change.

[P86]
He must have wandered around often enough to blend into Ningxia Province without the Seven Masters making any effort to hide who he was.

[P87]
Like Beggar Number One.

[P88]
*This is a hermit master?*

[P89]
Was this what it felt like to sink into a deep mire?

[P90]
The more I thought about him, the more baffled and curious I became. Then Jeok Cheongang moved his lips, apparently thinking much the same thing.

[P91]
—I thought I’d lived long enough to see hundreds of cartloads of madmen… but I’ve never seen anyone like this.

[P92]
—Your hair’s only just started growing back.

[P93]
—…Do you want to die?

[P94]
—No. But I agree with you, Old Master. I can’t make sense of him.

[P95]
—Could he be one of the Lord of Heaven’s minions?

[P96]
—The Lord of Heaven must have people left working for him. But if you were him, would you take someone like that on?

[P97]
Jeok Cheongang answered without hesitation.

[P98]
—Are you mad?

[P99]
—Exactly.

[P100]
—Even if I took a Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist to the head, I wouldn’t take a man like that as a subordinate. Assuming everything those vicious-looking bastards told us is true, of course.

[P101]
—But you already believe them.

[P102]
—That’s…

[P103]
His Sound Transmission trailed off as he turned his head. The instant the Seven Masters met his gaze, they went rigid as statues. Jeok Cheongang shook his head.

[P104]
—Yes, you’re right. I can tell they aren’t lying. No—they aren’t even capable of it.

[P105]
That much was plain to me, and probably to everyone else.

[P106]
But even if we concluded that the Seven Masters and Great Sir posed no danger to our side, the two of us couldn’t decide everything on instinct alone.

[P107]
—What will you do?

[P108]
Jeok Cheongang’s Sound Transmission reached me again. After a moment’s thought, I made my decision. I gradually eased up on the reins and drew level with the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang.

[P109]
“W-what is it this time…?”

[P110]
Ma Junggeol and his sworn brothers were frightened before I’d said a word.

[P111]
I studied them in silence, then asked, “How long would you need?”

[P112]
“What do you mean…?”

[P113]
“To bring the man you call Great Sir to where we’re headed.”

[P114]
“…!”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
